actions.label: Hand food over to guard/militia structures to run distribution
Refrain from skimming or diverting FWB food for guards and stop paying guards from refugee food
Insist on free movement of FWB staff inside the camp
Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
Press the Senior Militia Leader and Ministry of Defense to fund guard salaries and fuel
Grant FWB staff coordinated, escorted camp access with routes, gates and blocks set by Camp Admin
Have guards and militia organise and carry out the distribution
Permit FWB nutritional assessments under agreed security arrangements
Allow unrestricted free movement for FWB staff inside the camp
Supply ongoing food aid shipments to the camp
Coordinate entry routes, team size and schedule with camp administration

goals.label: Outside aid staff move freely inside the camp
Commander's personal safety and standing with the Senior Militia Leader
Refugees receive sufficient food and nutrition
Aid is documented and accountable to donor requirements
Camp guards/militia control food distribution
Commander faces legal or political consequences from abuse, riots or international attention
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
FWB neutrality, with no aid going to guards or militia
Food aid is diverted or confiscated by guards and militia
Food is distributed fairly without discrimination among refugees
Generators and power for security keep running
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Refugees stay contained and do not reach the capital
Refugees suffer abuse, violence or collective punishment
Refugees' nutritional needs are accurately assessed
Safety of FWB staff in the camp
Suspected terrorists or hostile actors benefit from aid or exploit access
The camp receives an ongoing supply of food aid
Food aid is used as currency or traded
Control of the narrative and information about the camp
FWB procedures and assessments cause delays and expose camp practices
Government and militia funding reaches the camp

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
